lifecycle.creation_reason: RC-004 of the KERNEL_BUILDER ready checklist asks for a cross-platform build check, and it is the sole remaining blocker on MT-118 and MT-144, both of which are otherwise complete and proven. It cannot be satisfied locally: cargo check for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc dies in the DuckDB C++ build under clang-cl because the MSVC install carries no ARM64 compiler, and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl has no musl C sysroot on this host so ring cannot compile. Branch CI is the only remaining path, and ten of its eleven jobs were failing for infrastructure reasons that had nothing to do with the product code, so there was no run to cite. This contract repairs the pipeline.

defects.observed: ##[error]Unable to locate executable file: pnpm. Please verify either the file path exists or the file can be found within a directory specified by the PATH environment variable.
defects.cause: actions/setup-node was configured with cache: "pnpm", which makes the action shell out to pnpm for its store path during setup. corepack enable ran as the next step, so pnpm was not yet on PATH. The job died about ten seconds in, long before any product step.
defects.fix: Move the corepack enable step ahead of Setup Node.js in both jobs.

defects.observed: error: failed to run custom build command for `libdbus-sys v0.2.7`. The system library `dbus-1` required by crate `libdbus-sys` was not found.
defects.cause: The Ubuntu runner image does not ship the dbus-1 development package, and libdbus-sys is a transitive dependency of the backend, so every job that compiles handshake_core failed at exit 101 in a build script.
defects.fix: Install libdbus-1-dev and pkg-config in each job that compiles the backend, folding it into the existing ripgrep install where one is already present.
defects.attribution_correction: An earlier draft of this contract also listed secret_scan and sbom_generate under this defect. The baseline per-job table shows both of those failed at their go install step, before any cargo invocation, so they were never dbus failures. They are carried separately as D-147-6.

defects.observed: backend-storage runs a [sqlite, postgres] matrix with a postgres:16-alpine service container, setting DATABASE_URL=sqlite::memory: on one leg and POSTGRES_TEST_URL plus DATABASE_URL on the other.
defects.cause: Stale configuration left behind by the storage pivot. Both backends were removed from the product, so even with the dbus fix these legs would test wiring that no longer exists and would keep the pipeline permanently red.
defects.fix: Collapse the matrix to a single embedded run, drop the service container and both env-configuration steps, and keep the storage conformance and MCP e2e invocations unchanged.

defects.observed: Database("HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must name the absolute _Artifacts root for embedded tests"), reproduced locally at src/storage/tests.rs:48.
jobs: every job that runs an embedded-store test
defects.cause: The embedded test backend resolves its store root only from an explicit absolute HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT, with relative and current-directory fallbacks deliberately forbidden. CI never set it, so any embedded test would fail on startup rather than on its assertion.
defects.fix: Declare HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT once at workflow level beside CARGO_TARGET_DIR.

defects.observed: The only Linux compile of handshake_core sat behind the frontend lint, dependency-cruiser and test steps inside the validate job.
defects.cause: Not a failure of its own, but a structural weakness: any frontend failure hides the cross-platform build result, and RC-004 then has nothing to cite even when the backend compiles cleanly.
defects.fix: Add a small cross-platform-build job that runs cargo check with all targets and all features on Linux and depends on nothing else.

defects.observed: secret_scan fails at the step Install gitleaks (pinned) and sbom_generate fails at the step Install syft (pinned), both in the baseline run 33666580708 and again in the post-repair run 33818193204.
defects.cause: Not yet determined. Both steps go install a pinned tool version under Go 1.22.4 and fail before any cargo invocation, so this is independent of every other defect in this contract. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
defects.fix: Diagnose from the completed run log and either fix in this microtask or hand to a named owner under AC-147-6. Must not be left unattributed.

defects.observed: validate fails at the step Docs check. The step asserts five governance documents directly under .GOV/roles_shared/: START_HERE.md, SPEC_CURRENT.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, RUNBOOK_DEBUG.md and PAST_WORK_INDEX.md.
defects.cause: None of the five lives at that path any more. START_HERE, ARCHITECTURE and RUNBOOK_DEBUG moved to .GOV/roles_shared/docs/, SPEC_CURRENT to .GOV/spec/, and PAST_WORK_INDEX to .GOV/reference/. The step had been unreachable behind the pnpm failure for as long as that failure existed, so the stale paths were never surfaced. Verified against the branch tree, not the working directory, because .GOV is a junction locally.
defects.fix: Point each assertion at the path the document actually occupies on the branch.

defects.observed: error: target `mex_tests` in package `handshake_core` requires the features: `duckdb-flight-recorder`, `test-utils`
defects.cause: All four supply-chain jobs invoke the mex_tests target without the features it declares, so cargo refuses before compiling or running anything. In the baseline this was hidden behind the dbus and go install failures in three of the four jobs.
defects.fix: Pass --features duckdb-flight-recorder,test-utils on each of the four invocations.

defects.observed: backend-storage killed by the runner with exit code 143 and the message: The runner has received a shutdown signal. Reproduced in two consecutive runs, 33818193204 and 33819481804, both around thirty minutes into compiling and before any assertion ran.
defects.cause: The invocation is --tests storage_conformance, which builds every integration test binary in the crate and only then filters by name. The crate has 393 integration test targets, so the job was compiling the whole tests/ tree, including targets that do not compile at all, until the runner died. This also explains why the job never reached a test result in any historical run.
defects.fix: Use --test storage_conformance and --test mcp_e2e_tests, singular, so each job builds exactly the one target it needs. The set of tests that actually run is unchanged.

defects.observed: error: target `storage_conformance` in package `handshake_core` requires the features: `test-utils`, exit code 101, in run 33820723714.
defects.cause: Cargo.toml declares required-features for both targets this job runs: storage_conformance needs test-utils, and mcp_e2e_tests needs duckdb-flight-recorder and test-utils. Neither invocation passed them. This was invisible until D-147-9 was fixed, because the job had been dying at the runner before cargo got as far as checking the target's features.
defects.fix: Pass the declared features on both invocations.

The MEX runtime executes gitleaks through the terminal service and the envelope comes back EngineStatus::Failed where the test requires Succeeded.

items.owner: The MEX supply-chain surface. It needs its own microtask; deliberately not opened here, because opening a second contract mid-flight would split this one's closure unit.
items.scope_correction: An earlier version of this entry grouped all four supply-chain jobs together and assumed they shared this failure. They do not. Once the required features were passed, vuln_scan, sbom_generate and license_scan all completed successfully. Only secret_scan fails, and it fails on gitleaks specifically.
items.progress_made: This is the proof that D-147-2, D-147-6 and D-147-8 are closed for all four jobs. In the baseline none of the four ran: secret_scan and sbom_generate died at their go install step, vuln_scan and license_scan died in the dbus build script, and after those were fixed all four were refused by cargo for missing required features. Three now pass outright and the fourth reaches its assertion.
